description: A port of S.A.M., the Software Automatic Mouth speech synthesiser written for the Commodore 64. Text typed into it is spoken at the output

params.text: How fast the words are spoken
The level of the speech at the output
How much of the voltage at the SPEED CV input reaches the speaking rate
How much of the voltage at the PITCH CV input reaches the pitch
How much of the voltage at the MOUTH CV input reaches the MOUTH setting
How much of the voltage at the THROAT CV input reaches the THROAT setting
How much of the voltage at the VOLUME CV input reaches the level
Reads the text as phonemes rather than as ordinary words, and swaps the colours of the text field over
Turns on the singing mode of the speech synthesiser
Switches on random sentence mode, where a sentence is put together at random instead of the text being read

inputs.text: A voltage moving the speaking rate
A voltage moving the pitch of the voice
A voltage moving the MOUTH setting
A voltage moving the THROAT setting
A voltage moving the level of the speech
A trigger switches the singing mode on and off
A trigger switches random sentence mode on and off

outputs.text: Sends a pulse when the text has been spoken to the end

notes: the text is typed into the blue field, which takes about 90 to 100 characters of ordinary text and rather more when phonemes are used, and the red lamp lights when a phoneme cannot be parsed
a change to SPEED, PITCH, MOUTH or THROAT is heard after the next stop and start, or at the end of the current pass when the text is repeating
a new module comes up holding the line Hello, my name is SAM., which is what it speaks until the text is changed
